summary.en: Plan a complete paper-card project, from a useful question to checks after the model is used.
summary.bn: কাজের প্রশ্ন থেকে ব্যবহারের পরে খোঁজ রাখা পর্যন্ত কাগজের কার্ডে একটি পুরো কাজ করো।

notes: Conceptual paper activities need no programming; teacher reference programs run on Python 3.10 or newer.

sections.title: A path with a return arrow
Run the whole recipe without a computer
Stages that are easy to skip
Keep the question connected to the action

practice.title: Define the decision
practice.statementHtml: Write Nana’s busy-morning question, decision time and label meaning.
hints: Make the action possible before opening.
practice.answerHtml: Before opening, predict whether at least twenty morning customers will arrive. The answer is busy or quiet. This helps prepare baskets; it does not classify customers as good or bad.

practice.title: A baseline count
practice.statementHtml: Count the always-quiet baseline’s mistakes on A–F and explain why comparison is useful.
practice.answerHtml: A, B and E are busy, so quiet makes three mistakes. Comparing a new rule with this modest guess shows whether learning adds useful information beyond a simple default.

practice.title: Missing forecast
practice.statementHtml: Describe how to handle a morning card with no recorded forecast without claiming it was dry.
practice.answerHtml: Mark the field unknown. Seek a reliable original forecast if available. Otherwise keep a clear rule for excluding or treating that record and state the limitation. Do not invent a dry observation to improve a pattern.

practice.title: The monitoring plan
practice.statementHtml: Nana tries the model for a week. Specify who records mistakes, a fallback and a reason to reconsider the question.
practice.answerHtml: Nana records each before-opening guess and the later actual count. He keeps spare baskets and can override advice using local information. Repeated missed busy mornings or a changed customer routine triggers a review of clues, examples and possibly whether exact basket counts would be a more useful target.

quiz.prompt: Read the morning table. Which practice cards would an always-quiet baseline misname?
options: C, D and F
Only A
Every card
A, B and E
quiz.explanation: A, B and E have busy answers. A quiet prediction disagrees with those three labels while matching C, D and F.

caption.en: Six invented training mornings; clues are known before the stall opens.
caption.bn: ছয় বানানো সকাল; দোকান খোলার আগে ইঙ্গিত জানা।

quiz.prompt: Using the six morning rows, which rain rule matches every shown training answer?
options: Busy when rain is not forecast, otherwise quiet
Busy whenever school is open
Always busy
Busy when rain is forecast, otherwise quiet
quiz.explanation: The three no-rain rows are busy and the three rain rows are quiet. School status alone fails on B and on C or F.

caption.en: Six invented training mornings; clues are known before the stall opens.
caption.bn: ছয় বানানো সকাল; দোকান খোলার আগে ইঙ্গিত জানা।

quiz.prompt: Why should Nana define “busy” before collecting labels?
options: So the model can choose any definition after seeing test results
So every card uses a consistent answer meaning
So the final labels can be ignored
So all future mornings become identical
quiz.explanation: A consistent definition, such as at least twenty customers, makes labels comparable. Changing it silently makes the task unclear.

quiz.prompt: Which clue is available before the stall opens?
options: The actual final morning customer count
The completed day’s unsold basket count
The recorded rain forecast
The final test score after labels are opened
quiz.explanation: A forecast can be recorded before the decision. Actual morning outcomes arrive later and cannot honestly guide an earlier guess.

quiz.prompt: What should a blank rain-forecast field mean?
options: It was definitely dry
The model may silently copy the desired answer
It was definitely rainy
The forecast observation is unknown
quiz.explanation: Unknown information must not be converted into a false observation. Explain how the missing card is handled.

quiz.prompt: Two genuinely different mornings share all recorded clues. Should one automatically be removed as an accidental duplicate?
options: No; similar records can represent different real events
Yes; identical clues prove the same morning was copied
Yes; a table must never repeat a feature value
No; accidental copies should also always be kept
quiz.explanation: Check event identity and source. Removing a repeated copy is different from discarding a separate day with similar conditions.

quiz.prompt: When should G and H’s answers be reserved for the final paper check?
options: After choosing the rule that best fits G and H
Before rules are selected using the practice pile
Only after rewriting both answers
After every card has been used for training
quiz.explanation: Early reservation keeps those answers outside selection. A pile chosen after inspecting outcomes can give a misleading check.

quiz.prompt: On hidden G and H, both truly busy, the rain rule predicts busy then quiet. How many mistakes occur?
options: Zero among two
Two among two
One among two hidden mornings
One among six training mornings
quiz.explanation: G matches, H does not. Keep the hidden count separate from training, where the rain rule matched all six.

quiz.prompt: What is the main job of a baseline?
options: Guarantee the highest possible score
Replace every need for checking
Prove the most complicated model wins
Provide a modest comparison that a new model should improve upon
quiz.explanation: A baseline helps judge whether extra effort adds useful value. It too must be assessed on suitable fresh evidence.

quiz.prompt: Several rainy mornings become busy after a bus-stop change. What should the use plan trigger?
options: Review recent mistakes and reconsider the data or rule
Keep claiming the old rule is perfect
Delete every new rainy record
Blame customers for differing from the model
quiz.explanation: Monitoring can detect changing circumstances. Nana may pause reliance, use a fallback and return to an earlier workflow stage.

keyPoints.en: Define what is predicted and when the guess is needed.
keyPoints.bn: কী আর কখন অনুমান করবে, ঠিক করো।

keyPoints.en: Collect relevant examples with consistent meanings.
keyPoints.bn: একই অর্থের প্রাসঙ্গিক উদাহরণ জোগাড় করো।

keyPoints.en: Clean records without turning unknown values into facts.
keyPoints.bn: অজানাকে সত্য বানিয়ে তথ্য সারিও না।

keyPoints.en: Reserve checking answers before comparing rules.
keyPoints.bn: নিয়ম তুলনার আগে যাচাইয়ের উত্তর সরাও।

keyPoints.en: Compare a learned model with a baseline.
Count useful successes and costly mistakes on fresh cases.
keyPoints.bn: নতুনে কাজের সাফল্য আর ক্ষতির ভুল গোনো।

keyPoints.en: Monitor use and return to earlier stages when conditions change.
keyPoints.bn: ব্যবহারের খোঁজ নিয়ে দরকারে আগের ধাপে ফেরো।

examQuestions.question: List the stages of the paper-card workflow and explain its return arrow.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Define the question, collect and clean relevant examples, reserve hidden checks, choose and train a model, test it on separate cases, then use and monitor it. The return arrow allows a failed check or changed conditions to send us back to the stage needing repair.

examQuestions.question: On training A–F, compare always-quiet and the dry-means-busy rule. Then compare them on busy G and busy H, where G is dry and H rainy.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Always quiet misses three training busy mornings; dry-means-busy misses zero. On the two hidden busy mornings, always quiet misses both, while the rain rule gets G right and H wrong. Hidden mistakes are therefore two versus one.

examQuestions.question: Design a four-role classroom activity that carries out the full workflow.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A question keeper defines timing and labels. A collector prepares invented consistent cards and flags missing entries. A learner compares a baseline and rule on the training pile. An examiner keeps separate labels sealed, records fixed predictions and reveals answers. Together they write a fallback and a monitoring plan.

examQuestions.question: Explain why a model score alone cannot finish Nana’s project.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The score describes a limited check, not the usefulness of every later decision. Nana must consider missed sales, available safeguards, changing routines and responsibility. A use plan with monitoring can reveal when the original model or question needs revision.
